verdict: Caution: lend selectively in Bhiwadi auto components only to gas-secured, OEM-diversified tier-2 units with tight monthly monitoring; avoid single-customer, gas-dependent plants.
title: Bhiwadi Auto & Auto Components: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Bhiwadi's auto-component units are press-shop and machining jobbers that convert steel, aluminium and gas-fired heat into parts for OEMs, and cash sits in the OEM's payment cycle, not in the plant.** Inputs are metal and energy; output is billed to a handful of large vehicle makers who set price and payment terms. Value sits in tooling and design complexity, not in commodity stamping, so pricing power is thin for job-work units and thick only where the part is design-critical [11]. Working capital is the real risk: gross current assets have averaged 160-170 days in recent years [10], so when a proposal lands, check the receivable days against that band; if debtors run past it, ask which OEM and what credit terms.

## What has broken now
**The local shock is energy, not demand: 400 factories are reported on the brink of closure with production halved and 25,000 jobs at risk [1].** That report is from April 2026 and describes a gas crisis forcing single-shift running [1], so when a proposal lands, check the unit's gas supply contract and shift pattern first; if it is running one shift on spot gas, ask for the landed energy cost per part. The state backdrop is weak: Rajasthan GST collections are -4.7% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, and electricity demand +4.0% against India +9.5% [D]. **Treat Bhiwadi as a stressed cluster inside a strong national cycle, not as a growth market.**

## Where the growth is
**National auto-component demand is running hard: IIP NIC 29 output is +25.2% YoY and +19.2% Apr-to-date [D], and peers confirm it.** Motherson Sumi Wiring grew revenue 46.7% to Rs 4,054 crore with net profit up 35% to Rs 223 crore [4]; Lumax beat Q2 2026 estimates and lifted its growth target [7]. **Pursue tier-2 suppliers feeding these diversified, EV-exposed chains, and avoid single-OEM stamping units exposed to engine and related parts, where obsolescence risk is rising as EVs spread [11].** Note the peer caution: margins may come under pressure even as volumes stay strong [6], and aluminium is squeezing margins at ASK [5].

## How to grow safely
**Structure for the energy shock: shorter tenor, tighter drawing power, and a covenant on shift utilisation.** Take monthly gas bills, electricity bills and OEM payment advices; if receivables stretch beyond the 160-170 day band [10], cut limits. Ask for the customer-wise sales mix; if one OEM is above half, ask for a diversification plan before enhancing. **Avoid units with debt-funded capex and Debt/EBITDA above 2.5-2.75 times [10].**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the gas bill and the shift register before the balance sheet.** A move to single-shift running, a missed OEM payment advice, or a sudden drop in electricity draw are the first signals; act on them the same month.
